card.title: Debts on the Scoreboard
card.instruction: Treat past wins and losses as debts. Let each new result change who owes the next favor, risk, or concession.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You beat me at darts yesterday, so you owe me lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. But you've just beaten me today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lunch cancels out. I owe you dessert for winning by more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Make it takeaway. I have to collect Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll collect her. A three-dart finish ought to cover a parent, not just a pudding.

mechanism: A converts alternating darts results and winning margins into an adjustable debt of favors.
confusable: Unlike a standing wager, each new result must change who owes what beyond simply collecting a prize.
comparison: S202-a enlarges repayment into collecting a parent; S202-b negotiates viewing obligations across rematches.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
